title: Dot Product of Two Vectors
notes: **Component form.** For a = (a₁, a₂, a₃) and b = (b₁, b₂, b₃), a · b = a₁b₁ + a₂b₂ + a₃b₃; multiply matching components and add.
**Geometric form.** a · b = |a||b| cos θ links the algebraic result to the angle, so comparing the two forms is a reliable way to find θ.
**Algebraic laws.** a · b = b · a, a · (b + c) = a · b + a · c, and (k a) · b = k(a · b); the dot product is NOT associative because a · b is a scalar.
**Self product.** a · a = |a|², which is why |a| = √(a · a) and why |a + b|² = |a|² + 2a·b + |b|².
**Exam caution.** The dot product of three vectors such as (a · b) · c is meaningless; use parentheses only where the scalar is multiplied by a vector.
summary: In components a·b = Σaᵢbᵢ; the product is commutative, distributes over addition, and a·a = |a|².
